_doc: Canonical hook WIRING manifest. Hook LOGIC lives beside this file (scripts/md payloads — the canon; per-harness copies are dead). harness-sync.sh renders this into each harness's dialect via build_hooks_obj(<harness>, <scope>): org scope -> <repos>/.claude/settings.json#hooks (Claude), <repos>/.codex/hooks.json (Codex), tools/droid/hooks.json -> ~/.factory/hooks.json (Droid); app scope -> <app>/.claude/settings.json#hooks stamped block (Claude only — no other harness has functioning app-scope hooks); machine scope -> ~/.grok/hooks/00-ac.json (Grok only: it discards passive-event stdout, so only PreToolUse guards + fire-and-forget loggers function there; its context stack is the generated ~/.grok/AGENTS.md rules projection instead). Pi has no declarative hooks (TS extensions only) — skipped with a warning. opencode has NO shell-command hook dialect at all: machine scope renders instead to <opencode-home>/plugins/ac-hooks.js, a generated JS plugin that wraps these same scripts (UserPromptSubmit -> chat.message part injection; PreToolUse -> tool.execute.before throw; PostToolUse -> tool.execute.after). The wrapper speaks BOTH block dialects, because our guards disagree: trauma_guard blocks with stdout hookSpecificOutput JSON + exit 0, while bead-capture-guard/skill-edit-guard block with exit 2 + stderr. Honouring only one fails open. opencode tool ids are lowercase (bash/edit/write), so the wrapper aliases them to the Claude-style names the matchers and scripts expect. Placeholders: {HOOKS} = this dir via $HOME/Repos path · {HOME} = $HOME literal. Event names are shared verbatim by Claude/Codex/Droid/Grok. Per-harness `command` objects express capability-gated content variants when needed. `timeout` (seconds) passes through to the rendered hook — REQUIRED on blocking hooks rendered for grok (fail-open, 5s default there). NOTE: regenerating Codex's hooks.json invalidates its trusted_hash — re-trust once via /hooks in the Codex TUI. Advisory hooks that write a once-per-session flag file declare `liveness_flag_dir` so drift-check can assert they actually ran (a hook that never fires is indistinguishable from one that fires and finds nothing). New advisory hooks opt in by default. The field is check-only — harness-sync does not render it.

PreToolUse cannot inject context here (exit code + stderr only, verified against am-edit-guard.py) — signals via exit 2 + stderr, once per session (session-scoped flag file keyed on CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, falling back to a daily key), never blocks the edit. `machine` scope (mirroring trauma-guard) is required for this to actually reach Grok — its build_hooks_obj call only reads scope=machine (render_hooks_grok), so scope:[org] alone would silently drop grok despite being listed in harnesses. `app` scope added 2026-07-30 (bd-klyfr) and is the one that matters most: registry SKILL.md files are symlinked into every app, so a spine edit almost always happens in an APP session — where org (repos-rooted only) and machine (grok only) both miss it. Explicit timeout because Grok defaults to 5s and fails open. `Bash` added to the matcher 2026-08-07 (Pi morning): the guard's own docstring requires BOTH entry points (a Bash redirect/tee/sed into skills/ bypasses Edit|Write entirely), and lint Check 18 probes that Bash case. Commit ac43f0a5 had hand-wired Bash into the RENDERED .claude/settings.json instead of here, so every harness-sync render silently stripped it — three restore/clobber cycles before the canon was fixed.

wiring._doc: Hard gate (Craig 2026-08-23): blocks `br create` / `br q` carrying no `origin:<skill>` label, so every bead records the workflow that created it. Supersedes the OPTIONAL `origin:` hint from plan 2026-07-16-1729-epic-bead-quality-invariants.md §3, whose §9 'convention, not a hard gate' ruling measured out at ~50% of 3818 beads with no provenance (1232 of them unrecoverable, so no backfill is possible — enforcement is forward-only from this date). Tokenizes with shlex, NOT regex over the raw string: a `br create` quoted inside a --description or a heredoc body must never false-block, and only the actual -l/--labels VALUE is inspected. Fails OPEN on unparseable shell — a guard must not wedge an unattended 3am ac-loop; the ac-bead-refine stamp-gate is the backstop for anything that slips past (including non-Claude harnesses). `origin:unknown` is legal and honest (mirroring the existing `discovered-from: unknown` precedent), so the gate can never deadlock an agent that genuinely cannot attribute a bead. `machine` scope is required to actually reach Grok (render_hooks_grok reads scope=machine only); explicit timeout because Grok defaults to 5s and fails open. Tests: hooks/bead-capture-guard.test.py, driven by lint.sh Check 18 (both directions — fires on an unlabelled create, silent on a `br create` quoted inside a description/heredoc, blocks an unsubstituted qa-shared twin placeholder).

wiring._doc: App-scope companion to `activity-logger`, added 2026-07-30 (bd-klyfr). A SEPARATE entry, not an `app` added to that one, because `matcher` is a per-ENTRY field: putting a matcher on activity-logger would also narrow the org render and lose its full tool_calls coverage, which `activity-report` consumes. Why app coverage is needed: the `memory_reads` table is the ONLY table with automated consumers — telemetry.py View 3b and, critically, dream-cycle/decay_lint.py, which proposes which memory facts are dead. org scope reaches only <repos>-rooted sessions and machine only Grok, so every read done in an APP session was invisible to memory decay — measured 72 rows over 34 paths against 458 fleet-wide memory files. Why the matcher: activity-logger is matcher-less, so app-scoping it as-is would spawn python3 on EVERY tool call in every app session (plan 2026-07-12 decision 2 rejected exactly that latency). Rows are only ever written for mcp__qmd__get / mcp__qmd__multi_get / a Bash command containing `qmd get|multi_get`, so this matcher is the complete set of signal-producing tools. Deliberately does NOT backfill tool_calls/subagent_completions from app sessions — those feed only the manual activity-report CLI and are not worth a per-call spawn. claude-only because app scope is Claude-only (no other harness has functioning app-scope hooks).

wiring._doc: App-local overlay slot for the per-prompt lane: an app MAY carry its own .claude/hooks/delegation-reminder.md and/or workflow-reminder.md (content files, tracked in the app repo); they are injected after the canon `pre-prompt-reminder`. Silent no-op when the files are absent, so the entry is safe fleet-wide. Exists because the stamped `hooks` block is re-rendered from this manifest on every sync — a cat hand-added to an app's settings.json is removed on the next sync — and body-compass-app had been carrying these two cats in untracked settings.local.json. Keep overlays small: the same hot-lane cost rule as the canon file applies. claude-only because app scope is Claude-only.
